text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said a parliamentary committee will be set up to prepare a constitutional reforms package to remove all the anomalies from the constitution.
- Iranian Ambassador in Islamabad Muhammad Mehdi Akhunzadeh said Iran was ready to participate in the conference on Afghanistan provided it is held under U.N. auspices.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto denied she was striving for a deal with the government for the release of her jailed husband Asif Ali Zardari.
- The Economic Coordination Committee of the cabinet has imposed a 10 percent regulatory duty on import of sugar with immediate effect.
- Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain said the law and order problem in Karachi would be resolved without deploying more paramilitary rangers or police.

- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto warned that if immediate steps were not taken to prevent economic disaster, Pakistan's fragile democracy would face a major setback and there might be a bloody revolution led by mullahs or other adventurist element.
- A Pakistan Air Force court martial sentenced Air Force squadron leader Qasim Bhatti to life imprisonment for drug smuggling.
- The government has approved a $40 million seven-year programme to downsize the Karachi Port Trust labour force by 60 percent and privatise some of its functions.
- U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan Thomas Simons signed an agreement with the government to fianance low-cost import of $10 million worth of U.S. soyabean meal in the coming year.
- The Central Board of Revenue has instructed the sales tax collectorate and the Income Tax Department to investigate the closure of 600 small- to medium-range industrial units.
- Two leading Pakistani banks have come to the rescue of Pakistan International Airlines to meet its immediate financial obligations in foreign and local currencies.
